# Results — Study 332 (Downside-Beta) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The Ang-Chen-Xing (2006)
downside-risk sort — each month estimate every stock's downside beta (β⁻, the OLS slope
on the market restricted to negative-market days) over a trailing 252-day window, sort the
cross-section into quintiles, hold the top-minus-bottom equal-weight long-short for the
next calendar month. Run on a large-cap S&P 500 basket of daily adjusted closes,
2005–2026, with an equal-weight market proxy built from the same panel. Pinned against a
**plain-beta sort** and the **relative downside beta** (β⁻ − β) control, plus a
random-partition concentration null. As-of **2026-06-19**; the in-progress month is
dropped. Match the fingerprints to confirm you hold the same tape.*

## Data stamp

| Tape | Window | Days | Tickers | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|--:|---|
| Daily return panel | 2005-01-04 → 2026-05-29 | 5,387 | 40 | `9da245a5bd56` |
| Equal-weight market | 2005-01-04 → 2026-05-29 | 5,387 | — | `a9c845a0f216` |

*Survivorship-biased: the basket is current large-cap S&P 500 names projected backwards
(opt-in guard). All numbers are upper bounds.*

## The headline — monthly long-short spread, gross

| Sort key | n months | spread (%/yr) | HAC *t* | ann. Sharpe | hit-rate | 95% block-boot CI (bps/mo) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|
| **Downside beta (β⁻)** | 250 | **+12.17** | **+2.56** | +0.59 | 0.59 | [+19, +176] |
| Plain beta (β) | 250 | +10.46 | +2.09 | +0.48 | 0.56 | [+4, +169] |
| **Relative downside beta (β⁻ − β)** | 250 | **−0.46** | **−0.14** | −0.03 | 0.48 | [−58, +50] |

- The raw **β⁻ sort clears the inference bar gross**: +12.17%/yr at HAC *t* = +2.56. Taken
  alone it looks like the Ang-Chen-Xing premium is alive on this tape.
- **But it is the ordinary beta premium in costume.** The plain-β sort earns almost the
  same (+10.46%/yr, *t* = +2.09), and the **relative** downside beta — the part of β⁻ that
  ordinary beta does *not* explain, which is Ang-Chen-Xing's own decisive variable —
  earns **−0.46%/yr at *t* = −0.14**, dead flat. Strip out plain beta and the "downside"
  story evaporates.
- The 2005–2026 sample is one long bull market with a positive market risk premium, so a
  high-beta long-short simply earns the beta premium. β⁻ rides along because high-β⁻ names
  are high-β names; nothing *incremental* to downside risk is paid for.

## Could you trade it? — cost sweep on the β⁻ long-short (net)

A monthly full-rebalance long-short turns over both legs; costs are one-way × NAV, charged
round-trip on each leg:

| round-trip cost (one-way bps) | net spread (%/yr) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0 (gross) | +12.17 | +2.56 |
| 5 | +9.77 | +2.06 |
| 10 | +7.37 | +1.55 |
| 20 | +2.57 | +0.54 |

At a realistic **10 bps one-way**, the net spread falls to +7.37%/yr and **HAC *t* drops
below 2** (+1.55) — and that is before borrow on the short leg, which a real long-short
high-beta book pays on the most expensive names. The monthly rebalance of a beta-sorted
book is heavy, the edge is a beta premium you can buy more cheaply elsewhere, and what
*little* downside-specific signal there is (none, statistically) does not survive.

## Random-partition null

Randomly drawn same-sized high/low partitions of the ranked cross-section earn a spread of
~0 bps/month (sd ~120 bps over draws), so the β⁻ sort's gross spread is real
*concentration*, not noise — but, as the relative-beta row shows, it is concentration in
*beta*, not in *downside* risk.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is a faithful detector

On a deterministic synthetic firm × day panel the same engine recovers a planted
downside-risk premium **only when one is paid**, and finds nothing when it is not — the
mandatory positive/null control proving the harness is a faithful detector (and a machinery
proof only, never market evidence):

| Planted `downside_premium` | β⁻ spread (%/yr) | HAC *t* | 95% block-boot CI (bps/mo) | signal? |
|---|--:|--:|---|:--:|
| 0.0000 (null) | −8.41 | −0.85 | [−224, +86] | no (|t| < 2) |
| 0.0025 (priced) | +30.02 | +2.87 | [+87, +415] | yes |

The estimated relative downside beta (β⁻ − β) correlates **0.92** with the planted
per-firm downside loading, so the sort really keys on downside risk when downside risk is
what varies. The harness works; the real tape simply has no *incremental* downside premium
to find.

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED.** The raw β⁻ quintile spread is real on this tape (+12.17%/yr, HAC
  *t* = +2.56), but the **incremental** downside premium — β⁻ − β, the variable that makes
  it a "downside" story rather than a "beta" story — is indistinguishable from zero
  (−0.46%/yr, *t* = −0.14). Real on the raw sort · None on the downside-specific part. On
  a survivorship-biased basket, which inflates the high-β⁻ leg.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net of 10 bps one-way the spread falls below the bar
  (*t* = +1.55), before borrow on a heavy monthly beta-tilted long-short. The tradeable
  part is the ordinary beta premium, which is cheaper to buy as plain market exposure.
- **Distinct from plain beta? — NOT SUPPORTED.** β⁻ − β earns nothing (*t* = −0.14); the
  whole premium is the beta premium wearing a downside costume.
